question: What is the main goal of antenatal care (ANC) services for a pregnant mother?

options.A: Determine the exact sex of the baby early on
options.B: Eliminate all physical discomforts during gestation
options.C: Monitor normal pregnancy and detect early complications
options.D: Guarantee a completely pain-free labor experience

explanation: Spotting issues early is everything! ANC is all about watching how the pregnancy progresses so you can catch and manage any little problem before it becomes serious. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: Why are nurses so important when pregnant women come in for prenatal services?

options.A: They are legally required to perform all surgical procedures during birth
options.B: They prescribe all medications independently of medical doctors
options.C: They diagnose genetic disorders without needing laboratory equipment
options.D: They serve as the primary contact to build trust and encourage hospital deliveries

explanation: You are often the very first person she talks to! Building that warm, trusting relationship makes her feel safe and much more likely to come back for a safe hospital delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: When is the best time for a pregnant woman to come in for her first booking visit?
explanation: Getting her in during the first trimester lets you set a solid health baseline right from the start and catch any early risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: Why do nurses need to provide individualized care instead of treating every pregnant woman the exact same way?

options.A: It ensures that all pregnant women take the exact same supplements
options.B: Medical doctors refuse to see patients who follow standard routines
options.C: Standard hospital guidelines are illegal to use in public clinics
options.D: Every woman has unique social, cultural, and physiological needs

explanation: No two mothers are alike! Factoring in her background, culture, and unique body helps you give care that truly fits her life. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a thorough initial prenatal booking visit?

options.A: To administer the final dose of the tetanus vaccine
options.B: To perform an emergency delivery for safety
options.C: To establish a complete baseline health and obstetric history
options.D: To finalize the birth certificate before delivery

explanation: Think of the booking visit as your complete roadmap. Gathering all her past and current health details helps you guide her safely through the rest of the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Why is finding out if a mother is Rhesus-negative during her first visit so crucial?

options.A: It proves the mother has adequate iron levels in her blood
options.B: It guarantees the baby will never develop newborn jaundice
options.C: It allows the nurse to schedule the exact day of delivery
options.D: It helps prevent potential blood incompatibility and isoimmunization

explanation: Catching a Rhesus-negative blood type early lets you plan ahead for special care (like anti-D injections) to keep both current and future babies safe! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Which two quick checks must a nurse do at every single antenatal visit?

options.A: Blood pressure and urine protein testing
options.B: Internal pelvic exam and ultrasound scan

explanation: Always check BP and urine! These simple routine tests are your best tools for catching early warning signs of pre-eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: What are you trying to find out when you perform Leopold's maneuvers on a pregnant client?

options.A: To check the mother's cardiovascular health status
options.B: To stimulate the uterus into early contraction
options.C: To determine fetal lie, presentation, and engagement
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the placenta

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just feeling the bump with your hands to figure out how the baby is curled up and positioned inside as delivery gets closer. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: Why do we routinely give iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant women?

options.A: To prevent iron-deficiency anemia and support fetal development
options.B: To completely eliminate morning sickness throughout the pregnancy
options.C: To speed up the onset of labor during the final week
options.D: To ensure the baby is born with a higher birth weight

explanation: A pregnant woman's body needs extra blood volume! Iron prevents anemia, and folate protects the baby's brain and spine development. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: A 28-week pregnant client comes in complaining of a pounding headache and sudden blurry vision. What should pop into your head first?

options.A: A simple reaction to eating too much sugar
options.C: Normal physiological changes due to increased sleep
options.D: Standard fatigue that requires drinking more coffee

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision combined in pregnancy are classic red flags for pre-eclampsia. Grab that BP cuff right away! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: What is the main reason we give intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) for malaria during pregnancy?

options.A: To boost the mother's daily caloric and protein intake
options.B: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To cure a chronic respiratory infection in the mother
options.D: To reduce placental malaria parasitemia and associated risks

explanation: In malaria-endemic areas like ours, IPTp stops malaria parasites from hiding out in the placenta where they can harm both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: Which medication do nurses rely on to manage severe pre-eclampsia and stop dangerous seizures?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is your go-to lifesaver drug for preventing and controlling eclamptic fits when blood pressure gets dangerously high. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: What is a major part of helping a pregnant client make a practical birth plan?

options.A: Arranging transportation and identifying the place of delivery
options.B: Purchasing expensive imported toys for the nursery
options.C: Choosing the exact college the child will attend later
options.D: Deciding whether the mother will return to work in a week

explanation: A good birth plan solves logistics! Knowing how she will get to the hospital and exactly which health facility she is going to prevents dangerous delays during labor. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Why is it best to start talking about family planning during antenatal care rather than waiting until after the baby is born?

options.A: Postpartum mothers are too tired to understand reproductive health
options.B: Hospitals forbid mothers from discussing birth control after birth
options.C: It is a legal requirement to purchase contraceptives before leaving the hospital
options.D: It gives parents adequate time to make informed choices about birth spacing

explanation: Bringing it up during ANC gives couples plenty of calm time to talk about birth spacing before the rush and exhaustion of newborn care sets in. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Why is the antenatal clinic card given to the pregnant woman to carry around herself?

options.A: Because clinics are not allowed to store paper records on site
options.B: To prove she has paid all her hospital bills in advance
options.C: To serve as a ticket for free meals at the hospital canteen
options.D: So any healthcare worker can review her history during an emergency

explanation: If an emergency happens away from her regular clinic, any nurse or doctor can instantly check her medical history right off her personal card! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)

question: What should you do as a nurse at a primary clinic if a patient walks in with a complication you cannot handle?

options.A: Wait until the next scheduled clinic day to ask a senior doctor
options.B: Send the patient home immediately with instructions to rest
options.C: Stabilize the patient, write a referral letter, and contact the receiving facility
options.D: Ignore the complication since primary clinics handle all cases

explanation: Always stabilize first! Then, make sure you write a clear referral note and call ahead so the bigger hospital is ready to take over her care smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)
